messages.subject: RE: [distance-sampling] survey effort (L)
parts:
The distance you walked is 6km per line, not 2km.  By walking each line 3 times, if you pool your data, you expect to detect 3x as many animals.  If you recorded effort as 2km per line, you would therefore overestimate abundance or density by a factor of 3.

 

Steve Buckland

 

From: distance...@googlegroups.com [mailto:distance...@googlegroups.com] On Behalf Of Solomon Chanie Alemu
Sent: 10 June 2018 17:54
To: distance-sampling <distance...@googlegroups.com>
Subject: [distance-sampling] survey effort (L)

 

I have got a bit confused after I had learnt a video from “online distance sampling course: Chapter 4 " demonstrating about determination of adequate sample size. It says:

 

"If a line is sampled three times,

-pool the distance data from three visits

-enter survey effort as three times the line length"

 

So, based on this note, for example, let me say that I run 17 line transects, 2km each,  along my study region. I visited each line 3 times (i.e., I did three sample walks for each). I know survey effort is total line transect but which total is correct is my question domain:

 

1)  What is my survey effort (L) then? Is it 17 times 2km only OR 3(17 X 2km), based on above example?

2) Which value 2km or 6km should be entered as “line length” in the “Contents of observation layer” under data layer of distance project, for each observation per line? 

 

I entered the 2km for each line, not the 6km! Am I right or NOT?

 

Your urgent help please!
